claims.explanation: Norethindrone acetate is a progesterone receptor (PGR) agonist, and its selective antiproliferative/cytotoxic effects are most likely driven by PGR expression: lines with high PGR (e.g., breast and endometrial lineages) respond to progestin-mediated growth arrest and apoptosis, while PGR-negative lines are resistant. The virtual-cell signature showing downregulation of MYC, PCNA, CDC45, CDK1 and other proliferation genes is consistent with PGR-mediated cell-cycle arrest, and the transcriptional similarity to estradiol/aromatase inhibitors supports a hormone-receptor-dependent mechanism. Additional selectivity may come from androgen receptor (AR) status, since progestins can cross-react with AR, and from loss of tumor suppressors such as PTEN that alter hormonal responsiveness.

features.basis: Drug is a PGR agonist; PGR-positive lines are the expected responders (literature and mechanism)
Progestins can cross-react with androgen receptor; AR-positive lines may show additional growth inhibition
Estrogen receptor-positive, hormone-dependent lineages (breast/endometrial) are enriched for PGR and progestin response
Virtual cell shows MYC downregulation; high MYC-driven proliferation may overcome progestin-induced arrest
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT and can bypass hormonal growth arrest, reducing progestin sensitivity
Cyclin D1 amplification/overexpression drives proliferation and may counteract cell-cycle arrest from progestins
Virtual cell shows CDK1 downregulation; high CDK1 reflects proliferative capacity that may reduce drug effect
Virtual cell shows PCNA downregulation; high PCNA indicates active proliferation and potentially weaker response
Virtual cell shows IGFBP3 downregulation; low IGFBP3 may enhance progestin-mediated growth inhibition
Virtual cell shows SPDEF upregulation; SPDEF is a hormone-regulated transcription factor associated with differentiation
Virtual cell shows FOXO3 upregulation; FOXO3 mediates cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis downstream of hormonal signaling
mTOR pathway activation via TSC2 loss may bypass hormonal growth suppression
